title: botrail project (.botrail)
description:
A `.botrail` project: one robot cell as text — robots and their
placement, obstacles, frames, motions, sequences, signals, sensors,
devices, scenarios, toolpaths, the I/O map and the parts pinned to all
of them. Every list is additive: a field a file does not carry is
empty. `version` is 2.

allowed_contacts.description: Process-contact exemptions, by names (absent in older files).

applicators.description: Spray applicators by name (absent in older files).

brushes.description:
Brushes — named process settings toolpath strokes run with (absent
in older files).

devices.description: Auxiliary devices (absent in older v2 files).

frames.description: Named world frames (absent in older v2 files).

io.description:
The I/O map's assignment layer — controller nodes, point → channel
bindings, declarations (absent in older files). The points
themselves are derived, never stored.

parts.description:
Part identity pinned to residents and groups (absent in older
files). The BOM itself is derived, never stored.

scenarios.description: Scenarios — named initial-state deltas (absent in older files).

sequences.description: PLC-style sequences (absent in older v2 files).

signals.description: Internal signal declarations (absent in older v2 files).

toolpaths.description: Toolpaths — Cartesian process paths (absent in older files).

ActionMsg.description:
Robot-addressed actions carry `robot` — the instance name, or `None`
for the scene's sole robot (ambiguous, and rejected, with several).

oneOf.description:
Start a named motion (its owning robot drives); await it with the
`done` condition.

Start a toolpath (continuous Cartesian process path) on `robot`;
await with `done`.
Linearly ramp joints (gripper open/close); await with `done`.
Grasp an obstacle at its current relative pose (instantaneous).

Release an obstacle where it is (instantaneous; the carrier is
looked up from the attachment).

Latch onto a moving part: taught poses ride its motion until the
track is released (conveyor tracking).
Stop following the tracked part (instantaneous).
Write an internal signal.
Command an auxiliary device (output coil).

AllowedContactMsg.description: One [`crate::AllowedContact`] by names: robot instance, link, obstacle.

max_range.description: Nothing lands past this axial distance [m].

standoff.description:
Distance the pattern was measured at [m]. The whole model is a
projection of that plane, so this is the number the authored
standoff should match.

transfer_efficiency.description:
Fraction of `flow` that reaches the reference plane. The rest is
overspray before the paint ever gets to the part.

Aspect.description:
The second facet a device or robot point carries when one name owns
several wires: a device's numeric commands and a robot's handshake.
Rendered as `name.aspect`.

oneOf.description: Indexed-transfer start (`Advance`).
Vehicle dispatch (`Goto`).
Vehicle station select (`Goto`, word).
Axis position command (`MoveTo`, word).
Speed command (`SetSpeed`, analog).
Robot start (motion / ramp / toolpath from another host).
Robot done / idle contact.
Robot program-number word.

AttachmentMsg.description: Attachment state of a grasped obstacle (see `ObstacleMsg::attached_to`).

robot.description: Carrying robot instance name; `None` means the first robot.

touch_links.description: Links allowed to touch the object (carrying link, gripper fingers).

Brush.description:
A process setting a stroke runs with — ABB's *brush*: which applicator,
at what fraction of its flow, and how the trigger is timed around the
stroke. Named on the scene, referenced from a toolpath's feed moves.
Analog process values live here, in the authoring, because signals are
bool: the PLC enables the gun, the program picks the brush.

flow.description:
Multiplier on the applicator's flow. `1.0` is the flow it was
calibrated at; a primer at half flow is `0.5`.

lag.description: Seconds it keeps flowing after the stroke ends.

lead.description:
Seconds the paint starts flowing *before* a stroke with this brush
begins — the programmed lead that compensates the fluid system's
delay, and coats the run-in. Zero is "opens exactly at the
stroke's first point".

CatalogRef.description:
A catalog package reference: the id as resolved plus, when known, the
dataset revision it was fetched at. `revision: None` is a hand-written
reference that has not been pinned (a part named by its catalog id
without going through `Robot.from_catalog`).

ChannelKind.description:
The channel type a point needs. Only `Di`/`Do` take part in the bake
and the URScript lowering; `Word`/`Ao` are table vocabulary — the
numeric commands a bool coil cannot carry.

oneOf.description: Always true — fire the actions and move on.
Every motion/ramp started by this step has finished.

The named robot has no motion/ramp in flight (interlock building
block).
On-delay timer from step entry (TON).
Level test of a signal.
Rising edge: on this scan, off the previous one (`-|P|-`).
Falling edge: off this scan, on the previous one (`-|N|-`).
A linear axis reached its commanded position.
Series contacts (AND).
Parallel contacts (OR).

Contact.description:
Contact type of the field device — documentation for the connection
table. Independent of `invert`: an E-stop button is an NC contact whose
healthy state reads high, so `estop_ok` needs no inversion.

oneOf.description: An external input, whatever the sequences do with the name.
An output coil, whatever the sequences do with the name.
A relay: no I/O even if only read (a constant flag).
Not on the table at all.
Send a vehicle to a named station; await with `device_done`.

Run a stopped conveyor for exactly `distance` metres, then stop
(indexed transfer); await with `device_done`.
Advects unattached obstacles whose origin lies inside the zone.
Moves the listed obstacles along `axis` within `range`.
Feeds parked carriers onto the line every `interval` seconds.
Returns carriers that reach its zone to `source`'s magazine.

A guided transport vehicle: drives station to station along an
authored path, carrying its body obstacles rigidly.

allow_reverse.description: May it drive a leg backwards instead of turning around for it?

tray.description: Load deck in the vehicle frame: pose plus full size.

DeviceMsg.description: A scripted auxiliary device commanded from sequences.

Electrical.description:
Electrical facts about a channel or a field device: what a lint can
compare when both sides state them.

logic.description:
The sensor output type a channel accepts / a device provides. Not
"sink"/"source": those words swap meaning between vendors.

FaultMsg.description:
A forced input of a scenario: a contact stuck at a value, or an open
wire (input level low — the functional value follows the binding's
polarity).

oneOf.description: An I/O node dropped off: every input wired on it opens.

FlashMsg.description:
A weld-flash binding: while `signal` is true, draw an arc flash at
`robot`'s TCP.

cone.description: Spray-cone size, `[length, radius]` in meters (spray effects only).

kind.description: Rendering kind; absent in older payloads (= flash).

spin_link.description: Link spun visually while the signal is on (cut traces).

FrameMsg.description: A named world-frame pose (mount point / teach reference).

ext.description: Lower-case file extension so the client can pick a loader.

url.description: URL the studio can fetch the mesh from (e.g. `/meshes/0`).

IoBinding.description:
One point wired to one channel. `(point, node)` is the key: a signal
fanning out to two controllers is two bindings.

auto.description:
Placed by `auto_assign_io` rather than by hand. Hand bindings are
never moved; `auto_assign_io(reassign)` drops only these.

device.description: The field device's electrical facts (voltage, output type).

field.description:
The field device on the far end (`"BEAM1"`, `"-B1"`, `"YV1"`) —
the connection table's other column.

invert.description:
Logical inversion between the cell's value and the wire level.
Projection only: the URScript lowering inverts its tests and
writes; the bake is untouched.

address.description:
PLC address as the controller spells it (`"%IX0.2"`, `"X02"`) —
a string; dialects live in the Python templates.

port.description:
The vendor's standard-I/O number, when the channel is one — what
the URScript lowering writes (`set_standard_digital_out(port, …)`).

IoDecl.description: An exception to the derivation, or an unmodelled point.

pair.description: The other channel of a two-channel safety input.

IoDirection.description: Which way a point faces, from the host's point of view.

IoMap.description:
The assignment layer of a scene: nodes, bindings, declarations. Stored
on the scene and in the project; everything else in this module is
derived from it.

IoNode.description: The controller box a program runs on and the channels it owns.

model.description: Part number / model (optional, a table column).

place.description:
A frame or obstacle name marking where the box stands (optional,
display only).

programs.description:
Sequences this node executes (`Plc` / `RobotController` only).
Programs listed nowhere are placed implicitly (one robot driven →
that robot's controller, none or several → `<cell>`).

uplink.description:
The controller this node's I/O belongs to (a remote I/O station or
a safety module hangs off a PLC). Beyond that ownership, a label:
no bus semantics.

oneOf.description:
A robot controller, possibly driving several arms (a two-arm
station on one cabinet).

Anything else — documentation only, cannot host programs or take
bindings.

IoPointId.description: `(name, aspect, direction)` — with the host, the identity of a point.

LegendMsg.description: A colour key for an obstacle whose colours mean something.

stops.description: Swatches top to bottom; an empty label is a swatch with no text.

color.description: Linear RGB, like every colour on the wire.

MaterialMsg.description:
Metalness/roughness, the pair every viewer botrail hands a scene to
already speaks (glTF, USD Preview Surface, three.js).

robot.description: Owning robot instance name; `None` means the first robot.

attached_to.description: Present while the obstacle is attached to (grasped by) a robot link.

color.description:
Display colour, linear RGB, from the scene file's
`primvars:displayColor`. Absent means "no authored appearance": the
studio then draws the obstacle as a neutral collision proxy.

enabled.description: Disabled obstacles render but are excluded from collision checking.

legend.description:
What the colours mean, when they mean something (a film map's
micron ramp). Absent for ordinary scenery.

material.description:
How the surface takes light. Absent means "no authored appearance",
same as `color`: the studio picks. Projects written before this
existed simply have no material, which is the same thing.

visible.description:
Invisible obstacles still collide; they are simply not drawn. Files
written before this existed have every obstacle visible, which is
what they meant.

Part.description:
What a resident *is*: identity and count, nothing else. Every field is
optional so a part can be as thin as `model="GVL-1200"` and still land
on the BOM; the catalog reference is what `Robot.from_catalog` fills
in by itself.

attributes.description:
Free attributes, summed by [`Bom::total`] when numeric. botrail
never validates them.

category.description:
BOM category (`conveyor`, `sensor.photoelectric`, `structure.fence`,
...). Overrides the category the resident's kind implies.

qty.description:
How many of them this target stands for. One resident is one part
by default; a group generated as twelve fence panels says 12.

PartAttr.description:
A free part attribute: a number (summable — `mass_kg`, `power_w`, a
price) or a text (`ip_rating`, a note). Untagged on the wire, so a
project file reads `{"mass_kg": 45, "finish": "RAL 7035"}`.

PartEntry.description:
One authored part pinning: `part` describes the resident (or group)
`target` of kind `kind`.

PartTargetKind.description:
Which kind of resident a part entry is pinned to. Kinds have separate
name spaces (a conveyor device and its belt slab may both be `belt`),
so the kind is part of the key.

oneOf.description:
Every obstacle under `<target>/` — an imported subtree, a generated
assembly. Counted as one line.

PathTargetMsg.description:
Serialized form (project files, Python boundary). Positions and axes in
the part frame; `spin` optional.

Pattern.description:
The footprint an applicator lays on its reference plane, as a *shape*:
the integrator normalizes whatever this returns so it integrates to
one over the plane, and [`Applicator::flow`] supplies the magnitude.
Coordinates are meters on the reference plane, origin on the spray
axis, `u` across the fan and `w` along it.

oneOf.description:
Elliptic dual-beta — the literature's standard fit for a flat-fan
air gun: thick down the middle, thin at the edges, and the extent
along `w` narrows toward the ends of the fan. `beta = 1` is a flat
top hat, larger is more peaked.

height.description: Full fan height along (`w` extent at mid-fan) [m].

oneOf.description:
Axisymmetric cone — a rotary bell or a round nozzle. `beta = 1` is
a flat disc, 2 is parabolic.

A measured static-pattern profile, sampled radially: what a shop
actually has after spraying a coupon for a fixed time at a fixed
distance. `radii` ascending from 0, `weight` the film measured
there (any unit — only the shape survives normalization).

PoseMsg.description: Position + quaternion (x, y, z, w), in meters / world frame unless noted.

base_pose.description: World pose of the robot's root link.

name.description:
Scene-unique instance name; `None` (older files) falls back to the
model name.

RobotSourceMsg.description: Where a project robot comes from.

oneOf.description: URDF XML (xacro already expanded), embedded verbatim.

USD stage reference (local path until asset bundling lands). The
application layer re-imports it via botrail-usd on load.

A catalog package (`Robot.from_catalog`): id + pinned revision for
provenance and script export, plus the fetched inner source so
loading needs no network.

manufacturer.description:
Manifest identity (maker, product name, category, numeric
specs) — what the BOM names the package by. Absent in files
written before parts existed; those lines then show the id only.

oneOf.description:
A tool welded onto a base robot (`Robot.attach_tool`): both part
sources plus the weld parameters, so loading re-runs the attach.

ScenarioJointsMsg.description: A robot start configuration a scenario overrides.

ScenarioMsg.description:
A named initial-state delta — one row of the cell's test-case matrix.
The unmodified scene is the reserved scenario `baseline`.

faults.description: Inputs forced for the whole run (absent in older files).

ScenarioObstacleMsg.description: An obstacle pose a scenario overrides.

ScenarioSignalMsg.description: An internal-signal initial value a scenario overrides.

SelectArmMsg.description: One arm of a branching step: its guard plus the steps it runs.

oneOf.description: Presence/area sensor: ON while a watched body overlaps the box.
Photoelectric beam: ON while the segment is interrupted.

SensorMsg.description: A pseudo-sensor: geometric test published as a read-only input signal.

mount.description:
Vehicle this sensor rides on; its geometry is then read in that
vehicle's frame. `None` (the usual case) is a floor fixture.

oneOf.description: Any robot's links trip it.
Only the named robot instances' links trip it.

SignalDefMsg.description: A user-defined internal signal (PLC internal relay).

actions.description: Entry actions, fired when the step becomes active.

select.description:
SFC selection divergence: when non-empty this is a branching step
— no actions, `transition` unused, the arms' conditions are the
outgoing transitions (first to hold wins, authored order =
priority) and every arm rejoins at the next step.

transition.description: The step completes when this condition holds.

brush.description:
Brush name (absent in files written before brushes existed,
which is the same as none).

name.description:
Defaults to empty: the Python boundary passes the name separately
(`scene.add_toolpath(name, tp)`) and overrides this field.

VehiclePathMsg.description:
An authored vehicle guide path: floor waypoints plus named station
stops (as waypoint indices).

VehicleTrayMsg.description: A vehicle's load deck, in the vehicle frame.
